questions.prompt: Forrest Gump, Big and Cast Away star which actor?
questions.connectionNote: Hanks plays commander Jim Lovell — the man who says the line.

questions.prompt: Which chemical element has the symbol O?
questions.connectionNote: Oxygen tank two exploded 200,000 miles from Earth — the reason the line exists.

questions.prompt: Hollywood's 'six degrees of separation' are famously measured to which actor?
questions.connectionNote: Bacon flew the command module as Jack Swigert — who actually spoke the words first.

questions.prompt: Which silver adhesive is 'like the Force: it has a light side, a dark side, and it holds the universe together'?
questions.connectionNote: The square-peg-in-a-round-hole fix: a CO₂ scrubber rebuilt from duct tape, hoses and a flight-plan cover.

questions.prompt: Which Happy Days actor grew up to direct A Beautiful Mind?
questions.connectionNote: Howard directed the film — and shot the weightless scenes in NASA's actual zero-g training plane.

reveal.summary: Apollo 13. An actor, an element, a party game, a roll of tape and a sitcom kid — every answer lives inside one story: Hanks and Bacon in the capsule, the oxygen tank that burst, the duct-tape fix that brought them home, and Ron Howard behind the camera. Houston, we have a problem.
reveal.ohMoment: Here's the twist the movie never tells you: nobody ever said it. The real 1970 radio call was 'Houston, we've HAD a problem.' The most famous line in spaceflight is a misquote — polished for the trailer.

editorial.notes: Canonical-phrase rule: the solve target must be the exact famous form, because players type from memory. Letter curve: M(1) → H(2) → A(2) → O(3) → E(3); full success reveals 11 of 21 letters (52%). The irreverence lives in the reveal (the misquote), not in the bonus question.
